Notice the language

What do they sell?

Blue = keep these wordsDashed underline = change these words
En el mercado artesanal de Otavalo venden artesanía.

At the Otavalo handicraft market, they sell handicrafts.

vender→venden

Vender means “to sell”. Venden means “they sell” here.

It is the ellos / ellas / ustedes form.

With ustedes, it means “you sell” (plural).

Who are “they”?

We mean the people who sell things at the market.

We do not need to name them. We use venden to say what people sell in a shop or market.

The people sell the products. The place tells us where.

Keep the pattern. Change two parts.

En place venden products.

En la tienda de Camper venden zapatos.

Activity B · Your own shopping habits

Where do you buy things?

comprar→compro

Comprar means “to buy”. Compro means “I buy”.

Compro libros. = I buy books.

You can leave out yo: compro already tells us “I”.

One person, one sentence

Choose a product and a place. Say one true sentence about yourself.

There is no single correct answer.

Use en for shops and markets.
For online shopping, use por internet.
Blue = fixed wordsDashed underline = your choices
1. What do you buy?
2. Where do you buy it?

Your sentence

One more step: from selling to buying
